deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a worked example of the axis-adjustment and calibration procedure for Gauss's circle instrument, described on the previous page. The instrument has a drum ('Trommel') on the third axis and an alhidade (index arm). The previous page defines B as the alhidade index reading when the line of sight lies in one plane with the second and third axes, and d = A + B as an instrument constant, where A is the drum index reading. The example is dated 3 Dec 1816; the target was the knob on Jäger's garden house. The distance is unknown, so the parallax p remains undetermined.

Raw readings (drum index I, A = 2°35'):
- h: 178°23'38'' twice.
- v: 178°22'19'' and 178°22'18''.
- 180°+V: 358°35'7''.
- 180°+h': 358°21'17'' and 358°21'16''.
- 180°+v': 358°24'56'' and 358°24'53''.

Adopted values (means of the repeated readings, minus 180° where needed):
- h = 178°23'38''
- v = 178°22'18.5''
- V = 178°35'7''
- h' = 178°21'16.5''
- v' = 178°24'54.5''

Observation model. Gauss writes 'eigentlich sollte seyn' (properly it should be) the following, with B the zero-point, p the parallax, a an axis/index error, b a further axis (inclination) error and c the collimation error:
- h = B+p+a-b
- v = B-p-a+b
- V = B+p+a-b+2c
- h' = B-p-a-b
- v' = B+p+a+b

The four equations h, v, h', v' have only three unknowns (B, p+a, b). Each unknown can therefore be obtained twice, and the two values are averaged:
- p+a = (h-h')/2 = +1'10.75''; also (v'-v)/2 = +1'18.00''; mean +1'14.375''.
- b = (v'-h)/2 = +38.25''; also (v-h')/2 = +31.00''; mean +34.625''.
- B = (h+v)/2 = 178°22'58.25''; also (h'+v')/2 = 178°23'5.50''; mean 178°23'1.875''.

Then, using the means, c = -1/2(B+p+a-b-V) = +5'42.6875''.

Finally d = A+B = 2°35' + 178°23'1.875'' = 180°58'1.875''. The page writes this last symbol so that it is read as 'A'; by the previous page it is the constant d.

My addition: because the design matrix has columns (1,1,1,1), (+1,-1,-1,+1) and (-1,+1,-1,+1), which are mutually orthogonal, these averaged double determinations are exactly the least-squares estimates. The residual mismatch is the same in every determination: 7.25'' between the two values of p+a, of b, and of B.

The right margin holds a second set of values: +1'22.4'', +0°57.6'' and +5'47.8''. These are probably from another series (another drum index or another day). I cannot check them from this page.

The following page uses B to bring the third axis into the plane of the first two.
errors: No arithmetic errors found: all the half-differences, half-sums, means, c and d check exactly.
The final line is labelled with what reads as 'A', but by the definitions on the previous page the quantity is d = A+B. This is a labelling or reading issue, not an arithmetic one.
The model equations are given without derivation ('eigentlich sollte seyn'). The signs are only internally consistent; I cannot verify them geometrically from this page alone.
c is computed from the mean adopted values, not from h directly. Using h directly would give (V-h)/2 = 5'44.5''. The choice is reasonable.

results.what: Determination of instrument constants (zero-point B, collimation c, axis inclination b, parallax/index p+a) by combining readings in reversed positions and averaging the redundant determinations
results.modern_name: Reversal (Umlegung) method for theodolite/transit instrument errors; averaging equivalent to least squares for an orthogonal design
results.usually_credited_to: Standard practice of 18th–19th century practical astronomy and geodesy (Mayer, Bessel, Gauss, etc.)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine instrumental calibration arithmetic from Gauss's Göttingen observatory and geodetic work around 1816. That the averages coincide with least-squares estimates is implicit, not stated, and is fully in line with Gauss's known methods.

checkable.asserts: design for (B, p+a, b) from h,v,h',v' is orthogonal, so the averaged double determinations equal the least-squares solution

transcription_corrections: The last line should probably read 'd = 180°58'1''875' (d = A+B per the previous page) rather than 'A = …'.
Marginal 'v = B-p-a+b': the minus signs are blotted, apparently corrected over plus signs, in the image.
The b value '38''25' has its first digit overwritten (3 over another digit); 38.25 is arithmetically correct.
Marginal values +1'22''4, +0.57.6, +5.47.8 belong to a separate column, apparently a different series.
